chunks: He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Dawood al-Hatmi reported to me by way of authorization, from Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Sulaiman ibn al-Ash'ath, who reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdan, who reported from Ibrahim al-Harbi, who reported from Sa'id ibn Dawood ibn (Abu) Zanbar, who said: Malik ibn Anas narrated to us from his uncle Abu Suhail ibn Malik, from his father who said:

He said: I was standing with al-Mughairah ibn Shu'bah when Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, rose to leave Madinah for Basrah, when Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, approached him and said: "O Mughairah, do you have an intention to do something for Allah, Most High?" He said: "And where is that for me, O Ammar?"

He said: "Join this call so that you may be with those who have gone before you, and lead those who are behind you." Al-Mughairah said: "O Abu al-Yaqdhan, how about something better than that?" Ammar replied: "And what is that?" He said: "We enter our homes, and shut our doors until the situation becomes clear for us, then we come out seeing clearly. Let us not be like the one who broke the chain wanting to laugh but fell into anguish."
Ammar said to him: "Far be it! Far be it! Ignorance after knowledge, and blindness after discernment?! But listen to my words: by God, you will never see me except at the forefront."

He said: Then Amir al-Mu'minin, blessings of Allah upon him, appeared before them both and said: "O Abu al-Yaqdhan, what does this one-eyed man say to you? For by Allah, he is constantly confusing the truth with falsehood and disguising it. He clings to nothing of the religion except what conforms to this world. Woe unto you, O Mughairah, indeed this is a call that leads whoever joins it to Paradise."
Al-Mughairah said to him: "You are right, O Amir al-Mu'minin. If I do not join you, I will never be against you."

key_terms.الأعور: the one-eyed - Imam Ali's epithet for al-Mughairah, who had lost an eye
key_terms.الدعوة: the call - referring to Imam Ali's call to support his legitimate authority against the rebels
key_terms.الرعيل الأول: the first rank/vanguard - Ammar's pledge to be at the forefront of Imam Ali's army
key_terms.يلبس الحق بالباطل: confuses truth with falsehood - a Quranic expression (2:42) describing deliberate obfuscation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about al-Mughairah ibn Shu'bah's neutrality before the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a dialogue between Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Mughairah ibn Shu'bah, and Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib before the Battle of the Camel (36 AH). Ammar urges al-Mughairah to join Imam Ali's cause, while al-Mughairah advocates neutrality. Imam Ali then appears and exposes al-Mughairah's opportunism, declaring that this call leads to Paradise. The hadith illustrates the political dynamics among the companions after the assassination of Caliph Uthman, when some like Ammar unhesitatingly supported Imam Ali's authority while others like al-Mughairah calculated their positions based on worldly considerations.
